summary: DuneMarch is a geospatial platform designed to track sand dune migration across Saudi Arabia and assess threat vectors to critical infrastructure. The system ingests NASA NISAR satellite data to compute the velocity and directional vectors of aeolian drift. By projecting these trajectories against a spatial database of transportation networks, municipalities, and industrial facilities, the engine calculates collision probabilities and estimated time of impact, factoring in dominant meteorological wind patterns. The architecture utilizes an AWS-hosted Python backend optimized for large-scale geospatial processing to deliver analytics to a React frontend. The resulting interface provides an interactive map allowing users to select specific assets and visualize their precise risk profiles and collision timelines.
details:
What It Does & How It Works:

RimalTrack tracks sand dune migration across Saudi Arabia's major desert ergs (Rub' al Khali, Al-Jafurah, Ad-Dahna, and An-Nafud) and forecasts when encroaching dunes will reach critical infrastructure. Using NASA Earthdata (earthaccess) with an EARTHDATA_TOKEN, the Python backend queries sequential NISAR Level-2 GSLC scenes over Saudi Arabia, streams only spatial subsets lazily with xarray and h5netcdf (avoiding multi-GB downloads on a 30 GB disk), and runs 2D FFT cross-correlation across 8 Dask CPU workers (with a calibrated SAR model fallback when offline). SQLite and GeoPandas project monitored Saudi Points of Interest (energy hubs, rail corridors, highways, desalination pipelines, and solar arrays) into metric UTM Zone 38N, combine local drift vectors with adjustable dominant wind forcing, and compute Estimated Time to Collision (T-min), collision probability, and High/Med/Low risk tiers. A FastAPI backend serves these endpoints to a React and react-leaflet web console featuring a Saudi Arabia GeoJSON mask, toggleable velocity vectors and Canvas heatmaps, wind-forcing sliders, 6-field POI popups, a searchable Risk Matrix with CSV export, and a 7-slide pitch deck.

Benefits & Intended Impact:

RimalTrack helps asset operators shift from reactive sand clearing to predictive maintenance scheduled around T-min, while running on a modest CPU-only AWS EC2 t3.2xlarge server without GPUs or large storage arrays.

Tools & Hardware:

Built on AWS EC2 t3.2xlarge (Ubuntu, 8 vCPUs, 32 GB RAM, 30 GB disk) using Python 3.14, FastAPI, earthaccess, xarray, Dask, SciPy, NumPy, GeoPandas, SQLite, React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, PptxGenJS, Esri World Topo tiles, and Google AI Studio for AI-assisted development. Key design considerations included zero-disk bulk streaming, BLAS thread control (OMP_NUM_THREADS=1), metric UTM accuracy, and shape-plus-color accessible risk markers.
